Subject: p99 spikes — checkout timeouts for live traffic

Sean / Aisha —

We started seeing a major spike in p95/p99 latency on our Redwood hosted endpoints since ~07:50 PST. p95 is up to ~900ms and p99 is spiking to 2s+ intermittently. Error rate (5xx) and client timeouts are increasing for our live payment flows; throughput hasn’t changed from our side. This is impacting checkout for a subset of transactions and causing retries.

Attached are a small sample of traces and a few request ids that timed out (request ids: fd7a3b, 9c1132, b5f9e1). Can you triage and advise ETA for a fix? We’re meeting with ops in 30 mins and need an update.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Fwd: p99 spikes — checkout timeouts for live traffic

Quick update from the runtime side — I’m seeing a sudden spike in prefix/KV cache miss rate starting ~07:48 PST across several host pools serving FinovaPay. Miss ratio jumped from ~0.7% to ~22% which explains the tokenization + kv fetch latencies bubbling into p95/p99. The error traces Emma attached show extended blocking while the system fetches cold entries from backing storage.

Preliminary hypothesis: a recent config change to the prefix-invalidation sweep window (rolled out last night to reduce memory pressure) appears to have scheduled a broad invalidation window for certain customer prefixes. That caused a concurrent rewarm storm across many workers.

Immediate proposed mitigations (in order):
- Roll back the invalidation sweep flag we rolled out (safe, small config flip).
- Trigger a targeted rewarm for FinovaPay prefixes (background re-populate, non-blocking path).
- Add temporary soft-fallback to serve stale KV for 1s to avoid blocking on backing fetches until rewarm completes.

I’ve attached a short log extract and a link to the p99 dashboard. If we rollback now we should see p99 fall toward baseline within ~15–25 minutes. Will start the rollback if approved.

Attachment: rollback_patch.diff
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/abcd1234/p99-latency?orgId=1

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p99 spikes — checkout timeouts for live traffic

On it — I’ve validated the cache-miss spike and the invalidation sweep rollout metadata. I’m initiating an emergency rollback of the prefix-invalidation change for the affected host pools now (change id: cfg-20261101-inv). Rolling in canary then global — starting canary in 2 mins.

I’ll also run a targeted pre-warm job for FinovaPay prefixes (non-blocking, rate-limited) and enable a temporary 1s stale-KV fallback at the edge to reduce blocking latency during the rewarm. Estimated stabilization: 20–30 minutes after rollback starts.

I’ll post updates here as the canary completes.

Marcus Lin
SRE, Serving Runtime

Emma / Carlos —

Thank you for raising this quickly and for the trace samples. We’ve identified a cause and executed an emergency rollback of a prefix-invalidation rollout that inadvertently triggered a large-scale cache miss/re-warm across several host pools. The SRE and runtime teams have applied a targeted rewarm and enabled a temporary 1s stale-KV fallback; our telemetry shows p99 falling back toward baseline over the last 10 minutes.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back invalidation rollout (cfg-20261101-inv) — completed at 09:15 PST
- Targeted FinovaPay prefix rewarm started at 09:18 PST
- Temporary 1s stale-KV fallback enabled at 09:20 PST
- Ongoing monitoring — will confirm final stabilization in ~20–30 min

Commercial proposal: we’ll apply a 10% credit for November’s usage for the affected window and provide a formal postmortem with detailed root cause and remediation steps within 48 hours. If this works for you we’ll issue the credit and publish the postmortem link as soon as it’s ready.

I’ll continue to keep you updated; please share any remaining request ids that still show issues.

— Sean

Redwood Inference
